prompt: Which of Iowa's largest food banks depends most on donations?
answer:
## Among Iowa's largest food banks, Northeast Iowa Food Bank relies most heavily on donations

Looking at the four largest Iowa food banks by total revenue (all FY2023, the most recent year with extracted figures — note: all four have filed newer returns not yet reflected in this data), contributions & grants as a share of total revenue:

| Organization (city) | FY2023 Total Revenue | Contributions Share of Revenue |
|---|---|---|
| **Northeast Iowa Food Bank** (Waterloo) | $21.0M | **97.3%** |
| Food Bank of Siouxland (Sioux City) | $6.75M | 95.2% |
| Food Bank of Iowa (Des Moines) | $47.2M | 96.0% |
| River Bend Food Reservoir (Davenport) | $39.1M | 92.9% |

**Northeast Iowa Food Bank** (EIN 42-1169648, Waterloo) depends most on donations, with contributions and grants making up 97.3% of its $21.0M total revenue in FY2023 (fiscal year ended June 2023) — and its program service revenue was just $474,535. It's also notable that this food bank ran a thin surplus margin that year (0.4%), underscoring reliance on continued giving.

Food Bank of Iowa is close behind at 96.0% and is the largest by revenue overall ($47.2M). River Bend Food Reservoir, despite being the second-largest, is comparatively the least donation-dependent of the four (92.9%), drawing more from program service revenue (~$2.6M).

**Notes on scope:** I searched "food bank," "food reservoir," and "food pantry" organizations in Iowa. Two other EINs named "Food Bank" turned out not to be comparably large: Linn Community Food Bank Inc (Cedar Rapids) files revenue of only ~$200K/year — likely a small, separate entity from the major Linn County hunger-relief operation — and Food Bank of Southern Iowa (Ottumwa) and Hawkeye Harvest Food Bank (Mason City) are much smaller (under $1.5M revenue) and I excluded them from the "largest" comparison. I did not exhaustively check every small-town "food pantry" (71 total matches), as those are generally local pantries rather than regional food banks.

## Among Iowa's largest food banks, Northeast Iowa Food Bank depends most on donations

Looking at the four largest Iowa food banks by total revenue in **tax year 2023** (all fiscal years ending mid-2023, the most recent year with figures for all of them — note newer returns exist for several but aren't yet extracted in this data source):

| Food Bank | EIN | FY2023 Revenue | Contributions & Grants | Contributions Share of Revenue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Northeast Iowa Food Bank** (Waterloo) | 42-1169648 | $21.0M | $20.4M | **97.3%** |
| Food Bank of Siouxland (Sioux City) | 42-1381516 | $6.75M | $6.43M | 95.2% |
| Food Bank of Iowa (Des Moines) | 42-1177880 | $47.2M | $45.3M | 96.0% |
| River Bend Food Reservoir (Davenport) | 36-3147342 | $39.1M | $36.4M | 92.9% |

**Northeast Iowa Food Bank** gets the highest share of its revenue from contributions and grants (97.3%), compared to roughly 93–96% for the other three — meaning it relies relatively less on program service revenue (fees for services, etc.) than its peers, even though it is smaller than the Food Bank of Iowa or River Bend Food Reservoir.

Notes:
- I searched for "food bank" and "food reservoir" organizations in Iowa; smaller operations like Linn Community Food Bank (~$200K revenue, mostly a 990-EZ filer) and Hawkeye Harvest Food Bank (~$1.4M) were excluded as not among the "largest." Food Bank of Southern Iowa's data in this source only goes through tax year 2017, so it was excluded from this comparison as outdated.
- Food Bank of Iowa, River Bend Food Reservoir, and Northeast Iowa Food Bank have all filed returns through periods ending in 2025, but this data source has only extracted figures through tax year 2023 for them.

prompt: Which of Iowa's largest food banks depends most on donations?
answer:
## Answer: Northeast Iowa Food Bank (Waterloo, IA) — relies most heavily on donations

Comparing Iowa's three largest food banks by revenue, all in tax year 2023 (fiscal years ending mid-2023, Form 990):

| Organization | Total Revenue | Contributions & Grants | Contributions Share of Revenue |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Northeast Iowa Food Bank** (Waterloo, EIN 42-1169648) | $20.99M | $20.42M | **97.3%** |
| Food Bank of Iowa (Des Moines, EIN 42-1177880) | $47.20M | $45.33M | 96.0% |
| River Bend Food Reservoir (Davenport, EIN 36-3147342) | $39.14M | $36.38M | 92.9% |

Although Food Bank of Iowa and River Bend Food Reservoir are larger in dollar terms, **Northeast Iowa Food Bank** draws the highest proportion of its revenue — 97.3% — from contributions and grants rather than program service revenue or other income, making it the most donation-dependent of the three.

**Notes on scope:** I identified these as the largest Iowa food banks by searching "food bank" and "food reservoir" in Iowa and checking revenue across all matches. Smaller organizations found in the search (e.g., Food Bank of Siouxland at $6.75M revenue, Linn Community Food Bank, various county-level food banks) were excluded as clearly smaller. Food Bank of Southern Iowa's data source only extends to tax year 2017, so it couldn't be compared on the same basis and was excluded. All three organizations compared have filed more recent returns (through fiscal year-end 2025-06) than this data source has extracted figures for (through tax year 2023), so these are the most recent figures available here, not necessarily their latest filings.
